newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: First NZ Capital launches corporate bond indices.
newsitem.headline: First NZ Capital launches corporate bond indices.

text.p: First New Zealand Capital on Wednesday detailed a group of newly launched domestic Corporate Bond Gross Return Indices.
"The corporate bond indices are designed to supplement the First NZ Capital Government Gross Return Bond Indices, which have become long-standing market benchmarks," First NZ said.

All indices are market capitalisation weighted and are defined by credit rating. There are "A grade", "A grade" for large issues longer than one year, "B grade", "A and B grade", "unrated", and "all corporate bond" indices.
Composite government/corporate indices have also been calculated.

Corporate bonds satisfying certain criteria are added to a portfolio in proportion to the total market value on issue for each bond. Coupons are reinvested into all the bonds, again in proportion to market value.
"Since each index measures gross returns (capital movements plus income), their value shows no tendency to decline sharply around coupon dates," First NZ said.
The bonds in each index are valued by Credit Suisse First Boston and the indices calculated daily.
Index performance data is published weekly, at the close of business each Friday and also on the last trading day of each month.
Each portfolio will be valued using closing market mid yield, calculated as a spread over government bond rates at 4.30 p.m. each day.
The indices will carry only fixed-interest securities issued in NZ dollars into the NZ domestic market. They may be senior debt, subordinated debt or capital notes.
